title: Hotkey silently fails after reinstall (stale Accessibility grant)
description: Ad-hoc codesign in install.sh produced a new cdhash each build, invalidating the TCC Accessibility grant on every reinstall; app then failed silently (print output lost). Fixed: sign with stable Apple Development identity, show an alert when Accessibility is missing, log via NSLog, relaunch app after install.
close_reason: Fixed: stable signing identity in install.sh, visible Accessibility alert, NSLog diagnostics, relaunch after install

title: Configurable storage location + JSONL backup/import
description:
User-picked storage folder so word history survives across dev builds, plus a plain-text safety net.

Design:
1. Replace ModelContainer(for: Card.self) with ModelConfiguration(url: storeFolder/cards.store). storeFolder lives in UserDefaults (@AppStorage); default ~/Library/Application Support/TranslationReview/. Settings tab gets a 'Choose storage folder…' button (NSOpenPanel folder picker). All builds open the same file — no import step needed for normal dev.
2. Schema-change insurance: after each save, also write cards.jsonl (Codable, one object per line) next to the store; add an 'Import from backup' action. Covers the real dev data-loss path: incompatible Card model change -> store fails to open -> current code falls back to in-memory and words vanish.
3. Future-only caveat: if the app is ever sandboxed, the picked folder needs a security-scoped bookmark. Not needed now.

Related: the in-memory fallback in TranslationReviewApp should probably not be silent-ish once backup exists — offer import instead.
close_reason: Implemented: fixed app-specific store path (~/Library/Application Support/TranslationReview/cards.store) with one-time migration of the legacy default.store, JSONL backup rewritten on every save, and automatic restore when the store can't open or is empty. Folder picker dropped — recovery goal met without settings UI.

title: Failed translation can be saved as the permanent translation
description: TranslationPopoverView.swift:31 — the Save button is disabled only while translation.isEmpty. The catch block sets translation to the non-empty string "Translation unavailable. Check the Chinese language pack in System Settings." on failure, so Save re-enables and that literal error text gets persisted into Card.translation and shown forever in Deck/Review.
acceptance_criteria: Save is disabled on translation failure (tracked via a separate success/failure state, not string emptiness), and the user can retry instead of saving the error string.
close_reason: Fixed: added separate translationFailed state; Save button is now disabled on failure instead of only checking translation.isEmpty.

title: Saved cards can be silently lost (no explicit context.save())
description: TranslationPanelController.swift:66 — save() inserts the Card but never calls context.save(). SwiftData's autosave is tied to app-active/resign-active notifications, but this is an accessory (menu-bar-only) app that is explicitly never 'active' (see comment at TranslationPanelController.swift:57). A force-quit, crash, or logout between saving a word and the next autosave trigger loses the card silently, even though the UI already showed success.
acceptance_criteria: Saving a word calls context.save() (or equivalent explicit persistence) immediately after insert, and a save failure is surfaced rather than swallowed.
close_reason: Fixed: save() now calls try container.mainContext.save() explicitly after insert, instead of relying on autosave (which never fires for an accessory app).

title: Clipboard fallback can destroy non-text clipboard contents
description: SelectionService.swift:49 — selectedTextViaCopy() reads pasteboard.string(forType: .string) before issuing synthetic Cmd+C. If the clipboard held an image/file/RTF item with no .string representation, previousText is nil, but clearContents() still runs and nothing is restored — the user's original clipboard content is permanently gone. Occurs when using the Accessibility-API fallback path over Electron apps (Claude, Chrome, Slack per the doc comment).
acceptance_criteria: Non-text clipboard contents are preserved: either skip clear/restore when there is no string to save, or snapshot/restore all pasteboard types, not just .string.
close_reason: Fixed: selectedTextViaCopy() now snapshots all pasteboard items/types before the synthetic Cmd+C and restores them via writeObjects(), instead of only capturing/restoring the .string representation.

title: Smarter spaced-repetition schedule for long-term retention
description:
Future feature: improve how the app helps users remember words long-term. Research summary (Nov 2026):
- Spaced repetition with expanding intervals + active recall (reveal-then-grade, which the app already does) is the proven core. Meta-analyses confirm it beats massed study at equal time.
- Algorithm tiers: fixed expanding intervals (current 1/3/7) < SM-2 (classic Anki) < FSRS (modern, now Anki's recommended scheduler; open-source implementations exist). FSRS mainly reduces review workload at equal retention; for a casual personal tool the practical difference vs. a good fixed ladder is small.
- Recommended increments, in order of effort: (1) extend the ladder to 1/3/7/14/30 days instead of graduating after 7 — cheapest, big retention win; (2) add an 'Easy/Hard' grade that skips/halves a stage; (3) adopt FSRS (swift port or reimplement the ~20-line scheduler) only if review load becomes annoying.
- Keep ReviewScheduler pure/unit-tested as it is now; any algorithm swap stays behind that enum.
Depends on daily-review-notification flow being in place so due cards actually get seen.

title: Force-cast in Accessibility selection lookup can crash the hotkey handler
description: SelectionService.swift:28 — selectedTextViaAccessibility() force-casts the focused UI element (focused as! AXUIElement) instead of using a safe conditional cast. If AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue ever returns a focused element whose underlying CFType doesn't bridge to AXUIElement, the force cast traps and crashes the whole app from a background hotkey handler instead of falling back to the clipboard-copy path.
acceptance_criteria: The cast uses as? with a guard that falls through to the clipboard-copy fallback on failure, instead of crashing.
close_reason: Fixed: replaced force cast with an explicit CFGetTypeID check (Swift can't do a real conditional downcast on CF types) before the AXUIElement cast.

title: App launch crashes if the SwiftData store can't be opened
description: TranslationReviewApp.swift:12 — ModelContainer creation uses try!. A future schema change without a migration plan, or a corrupted/locked store file (e.g. after a crash mid-write), makes ModelContainer(for: Card.self) throw, crashing the app on every launch with no recovery path.
acceptance_criteria: ModelContainer creation failure is handled gracefully (e.g. fallback store, user-facing error, or recovery UI) instead of crashing via try!.
close_reason: Fixed: ModelContainer creation now falls back to an in-memory store on failure instead of crashing via try!.

title: Hotkey re-entrancy races the panel and the shared pasteboard
description: TranslationPanelController.swift:16 — the hotkey handler spawns a new unguarded Task on every keydown with no re-entrancy check. Two rapid ⌥⌘T presses (or key-repeat) run translateSelection() concurrently: the second show() overwrites self.panel (line 62) without closing the first, leaving a stray floating panel, while both calls' selectedTextViaCopy() invocations concurrently read/clear/restore NSPasteboard.general, corrupting the clipboard-restore logic.
acceptance_criteria: A second hotkey press while a translation is already in flight is ignored or queued, not run concurrently. The old panel is closed before a new one is shown.
close_reason: Fixed: added isTranslating re-entrancy guard (with defer) in translateSelection(), and show() now closes any existing panel before presenting a new one.
